title: QA / SDET
description: Test the details. Protect the experience.
audience: Career-switchers exploring a structured technical path.
Learners able to practice regularly and contribute to supervised projects.
prerequisites: Basic computer literacy and confidence navigating web applications.
No prior programming experience is assumed in this illustrative outline.

modules.title: Quality foundations
modules.summary: Think critically about behavior, risk, and evidence.
weeklyTopics: Software delivery and the tester’s role
Test design, boundaries, and equivalence classes
Defect reports, exploratory testing, and accessibility
Agile collaboration and practical test planning

modules.title: Programming for testing
modules.summary: Build a working foundation before automating.
weeklyTopics: TypeScript values, control flow, and functions
Collections, objects, and data handling
Git, branching, and collaborative reviews
Debugging, asynchronous code, and small utilities

modules.title: Browser automation
modules.summary: Create maintainable checks for user journeys.
weeklyTopics: Playwright setup, locators, and assertions
Fixtures, isolation, and reliable test data
Forms, network control, and authentication tests
Page abstractions, traces, and failure investigation

modules.title: APIs and data
modules.summary: Check the boundaries between services.
weeklyTopics: HTTP, contracts, and API test design
API automation and negative-path checks
SQL foundations and data verification
Integration testing and environment strategy

modules.title: Delivery and nonfunctional quality
modules.summary: Make checks useful in a delivery pipeline.
weeklyTopics: CI pipelines, artifacts, and test reporting
Risk-based regression and test-suite maintenance
Performance and security testing fundamentals
Accessibility checks and quality review practices

modules.title: Supervised product sprint
modules.summary: Contribute clear evidence and explain your decisions.
weeklyTopics: HireFlow test strategy and scoped backlog
Implement and review product checks
Investigate defects and present sprint evidence
Portfolio walkthrough and technical interview practice

title: Full-Stack Development
description: Bring the interface and the system together.
audience: Career-switchers exploring a structured technical path.
Learners able to practice regularly and contribute to supervised projects.
prerequisites: Basic computer literacy and time for regular coding practice.
This illustrative beginner outline starts with web and programming foundations.
skills: Design typed APIs and relational data
Test, deploy, and explain a product feature

modules.title: Web foundations
modules.summary: Understand how a browser becomes a product interface.
weeklyTopics: Semantic HTML and accessible forms
CSS layout and responsive composition
JavaScript values, functions, and browser events
Git, debugging, and a small interactive page

modules.title: Application programming
modules.summary: Write code that stays understandable as it grows.
weeklyTopics: TypeScript types, objects, and modules
Asynchronous JavaScript and HTTP requests
Error handling and practical unit tests
Application structure and collaborative code review

modules.title: Frontend product development
modules.summary: Compose interfaces around user tasks.
weeklyTopics: React components, state, and composition
Forms, validation, and accessible feedback
Routing, server rendering, and data fetching
UI testing, loading states, and responsive reviews

modules.title: Backend and relational data
modules.summary: Build secure boundaries behind the interface.
weeklyTopics: Node.js API design and input validation
SQL, relational modeling, and migrations
Authentication, roles, and resource ownership
Integration tests and transactional operations

modules.title: Reliable delivery
modules.summary: Move a feature from local code to an operated service.
weeklyTopics: Testing across the stack and CI automation
Deployment configuration and secret handling
Performance profiling and practical observability
API hardening and failure recovery

modules.title: Supervised product sprint
modules.summary: Build a feature you can explain from end to end.
weeklyTopics: HireFlow feature scope and data contracts
Implement, test, and review the feature
Resolve review feedback and demonstrate the product
Portfolio documentation and technical interview practice

title: AI Engineering
audience: Career-switchers exploring a structured technical path.
Learners able to practice regularly and contribute to supervised projects.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of Python functions, collections, and debugging.
Comfort with basic algebra, data handling, and HTTP/API concepts.
A reviewed prerequisite assessment is required before admission; this draft is not an approved admissions policy.
skills: Build and evaluate an AI feature
Use retrieval and model APIs responsibly
Test, observe, and explain an AI application

modules.title: Python and data readiness
modules.summary: Check foundations before building model-driven behavior.
weeklyTopics: Python readiness review and prerequisite assessment
Data cleaning, typing, and reproducible notebooks
Linear algebra and probability concepts for applications
APIs, Git, and small testable Python services

modules.title: Machine learning foundations
modules.summary: Understand evaluation rather than relying on a demo.
weeklyTopics: Features, training data, and leakage
Regression, classification, and baseline models
Validation splits and meaningful evaluation metrics
Error analysis, bias, and documentation

modules.title: LLM application foundations
modules.summary: Connect models to bounded product tasks.
weeklyTopics: Model APIs, structured outputs, and prompting
Input validation, retries, and cost awareness
Embeddings and semantic retrieval concepts
Retrieval pipelines and grounding checks

modules.title: Evaluation and safeguards
modules.summary: Make behavior inspectable and failure-aware.
weeklyTopics: Build task-specific evaluation datasets
Measure relevance and compare alternatives
Prompt injection awareness and sensitive-data handling
Tool boundaries, human review, and adversarial cases

modules.title: Deploying AI features
modules.summary: Operate a small feature with practical controls.
weeklyTopics: API integration and background processing
Observability, latency, and usage budgets
Versioning prompts, data, and evaluation results
Testing, deployment, and rollback practices

modules.title: Supervised product sprint
modules.summary: Contribute an evaluated feature, not an unsupported promise.
weeklyTopics: HireFlow AI feature scope and acceptance criteria
Implement a bounded prototype and evaluations
Review limitations, failures, and product integration
Portfolio evidence and technical interview practice
